why.title: Rates are scattered, and you can't tell how old they are
why.body: Today you dig through scattered messages to find a rate: one number each, no time, nothing to compare it with. NetRate puts every office's rate side by side, in the order of the money you actually get, and shows how many minutes ago each rate was posted.
points: Compared on the effective rate, fee included; not the rate an office advertises.
Every rate shows its age, and old rates fade.
The rank is just a number; no office gets a special frame or colour.

steps.title: Type your amount and currency
steps.body: Say 1,000 pounds. Pick the rate type and the direction too: Send to Iran or Receive from Iran.

steps.title: See the offices in order
steps.body: The list is ordered by Highest payout, and every rate shows how many minutes ago it was posted.

steps.title: Contact the office directly
steps.body: Call, message or get directions; the deal is directly between you and the office, and NetRate never moves money.

dark.title: Three themes, all complete
dark.body: NetRate changes with you: warm, cream Dusk, true Black for the night and White for the day. Just now, as you scrolled, the page went dark with the phone.

features.title: Everything you need to decide

items.title: Rates
items.body: Switch the direction, pick the rate type (cash, bank transfer, official invoice) and the currency. It always compares the effective rate, fee included.

items.title: Offices
items.body: Search, pick your city and show only offices that are “Open now” or “Verified”. Every office page has its branches, chart, opening hours and reviews.

items.title: A complete chart
items.body: From a week to a year, up to five offices side by side, on the Persian or Gregorian calendar. Learning mode explains what the chart says. NetRate doesn't predict rates.

items.title: Rate alerts
items.body: Say what to watch (the market's highest rate, the average or one office) and when to tell you. The whole alert is written as one sentence under the form, and each alert tells you at most once a day.

features.note: No account needed to see rates, the list, the chart or search; an account is only for alerts, saved offices and reviews.

light.title: For daylight
light.body: A clean, high-contrast White theme. All three themes are in the app and the choice is yours; here too, you can fix the theme from the top of the page.

honest.title: It tells you the truth, even when there's no news

items.title: Sundays, the week in summary
items.body: Most UK offices are closed on Sundays. The app doesn't go empty: it shows last week's summary, and the offices that are open come to the top.

items.title: Expired rates fade, with a label
items.body: A rate that wasn't updated today fades, gets an “Expired” label and is never counted in the order or the average. No number comes without its age.

items.title: Offline, still in the know
items.body: When you lose your connection, a bar at the top tells you how many minutes ago the last rates were posted.

items.title: English and Persian
items.body: The app is complete in two languages, each with its own numerals and reading direction.

widget.title: Home screen and lock screen widgets
widget.body: See the rate without opening the app: home screen widgets on iPhone and Android, and a lock screen widget on iPhone. The design is still in progress.

trust.title: Why you can trust NetRate
trust.statement: NetRate is not an exchange office and never moves money.
trust.statementBody: The offices post the rates themselves, for information only; for a firm rate, contact the office before you deal.

items.title: Every rate shows its age
items.body: The offices post their own rates, and you see how many minutes ago each one was posted.

items.title: One “Verified” badge
items.body: Vouched for by two verified offices, or checked by company number and AML. The badge can't be bought.

items.title: Reviews are moderated
items.body: Every review is checked before it's published.

items.title: No account needed
items.body: Seeing rates, the list, the chart and search needs no account.

items.title: We don't ask for your location
Account deletion has a public address
items.body: Whenever you want, your account and its data are deleted.

offices.title: Post your rate every day from a simple panel
offices.body: The NetRate web panel works well on a phone, and you get a reminder to post your rate. Your rate appears just like the office on this phone.

items.title: Post your rate, with reminders
items.body: Every day from your phone or computer, in seconds.

items.title: A rate card with your logo
items.body: Turn that rate into a polished card, as an image or text, for your channel and social media.

items.title: Daily Featured spot
items.body: Limited and bought day by day, always clearly labelled “Featured”.

items.title: Reports and stats
items.body: Weekly and monthly reports and full statistics.

items.a: No. NetRate is not an exchange office and never moves any money. It only puts the rates the offices themselves post side by side; the deal is directly between you and the office.

Your money never reaches us, so its safety depends on the office you deal with. The “Verified” badge, user ratings and “Always up to date” on each office's page are there for exactly that; look at them before you deal.
Each office has its own rate and fee, and its cash, bank transfer and official invoice rates differ too. That's why, once you type an amount, the order is by the money you get after the fee.
The rate an office gives for a transfer with its official invoice, for when you need formal proof of payment. It usually differs a little from cash and bank transfer.

items.q: What does an expired rate mean?
items.a: A rate the office hasn't updated today. It stays for one day, faded and labelled, then goes; it's never counted in the order or the average.
In one of two equal ways: two active verified offices vouch for it, or it gives its company number and AML number and our team checks them. The badge can't be bought and has only one level.

items.q: Why are there so few rates on Sunday?
items.a: Most UK offices are closed on Sundays. That day you see last week's summary, and the offices that are open come to the top of the list.

items.q: Do I need an account to see rates?
items.a: No. Rates, the office list, the chart and search all work without an account. You only need one for rate alerts, saved offices and writing reviews.
